newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: North's IOCC sees higher 1997 sales.
newsitem.headline: North's IOCC sees higher 1997 sales.

text.p: Australian miner North Ltd's newly acquired subsidiary, the Iron Ore Co of Canada (IOCC), has forecast improved sales in 1997, according to the annual report of a minority shareholder.

The report of IOCC's 12 percent shareholder, the Labrador Iron Ore Royalty Income Fund, shows IOCC posted a 25 percent rise in net income to US$41.9 million in 1996, struck on six percent growth in sales revenue to US$433.7 million.
IOCC will be hit in 1997 by a one percent fall in the negotiated price it receives for its iron ore pellets, but this will be more than offset by higher sales volume, it said.
In 1996, IOCC sold 10.5 million tonnes of iron ore pellets, six percent more than in 1995, and 4.2 million tonnes of iron ore concentrate, 12 percent less than 1995, it said.
"The existence of favourable economic condictions in North America and world markets generally is positive for iron ore markets in 1997," Labrador's report said.

"IOC expects sales volume of pellets and concentrate to exceed 1996 levels. This increased volume should more than offset the effect of the one percent price reduction negotiated for 1997 pellet sales," it said.

In January, North paid US$230 million for a 59.3 percent stake in one of Canada's biggest iron ore producers, positioning North to capitalise on electric arc steel-making, which is emerging a strong competition to traditional steel-making.
North said last month it wanted to spend about A$2 billion to raise its profile in the iron ore industry.
Among its plans, are proposals to restart IOCC's idle pellet plant at the port of Sept-Iles in Quebec province, and possibly to reopen another pellet plant at Cape Lambert in Australia.
North has said it is looking at ways of upgrading its orebody deposits at its West Angelas and Robe River operations in Western Australia.
